robot: Unitree G1 humanoid, 29 joints (legs 12, waist 3, arms 7 + 7), 1.32 m; Unitree's walking policy and a running policy built in; fist pads on both wrists

frame.suite: heading only: the yaw of the pelvis IMU in the venue's world frame; the robot senses no position, so x and y stay 0
frame.base_text: the robot base frame: on the floor under the pelvis, +X the way the pelvis faces at the start of the call, +Y left, +Z up (only the heading is sensed, from the pelvis IMU)

torso.note: the waist (yaw, roll, pitch), joint targets through the joints type

left.note: 7 joints: shoulder pitch, roll, yaw, elbow, wrist roll, pitch, yaw; joint targets through the joints type

right.note: 7 joints: shoulder pitch, roll, yaw, elbow, wrist roll, pitch, yaw; joint targets through the joints type

legs.note: 12 joints (left hip pitch, roll, yaw, knee, ankle pitch, roll; then the right leg's) through the joints type: the default gains, nothing balances the robot

resets.note: Embodied Olympics allows 5 resets (describe_robot: resets): each starts a new attempt from the same start; only the last attempt is graded, and a success ends the run.

notes: Joint targets are absolute angles (rad); a target moves at most the joint's speed limit per 10 ms step. On the beam every part (legs, torso = the waist, arms) takes joint targets through the `joints` type at the default gains, the way the robot starts (held by a `lowcmd` row of those targets); nothing balances the robot but your own targets. A `stand` row moves the legs to the normal stance and a `walk` row starts the normal gait: both put the feet beside the beam, so locomote is not offered here. move_robot and joint rows start from the last `joints` row sent through these tools (at the start of an attempt: the start targets); other gains, velocities and feed-forward torques are the native `lowcmd` type (execute_trajectory space native; layouts and bounds of every type (stand, walk, run, run_arms, joints, lowcmd, walk_falcon, walk_agile) in describe_robot). Between calls the robot is frozen: time passes only inside calls. There is no end-effector pose command: describe_robot's spec_file (robot_facts) has each joint's range, speed and torque limits, default gains and the stance. The robot senses no position: the state shows its heading (the pelvis IMU's yaw) only, and locomote's displacement reports the turn (dyaw), while dx and dy stay 0: judge distances from the cameras. Once an attempt is over, results carry the referee's call (outcome, stages_reached of stages_total).
